highlights.text: Sometimes I think there is more rest in that place between wakefulness and sleep than there is in true sleep. The mind walks in the twilight of both states, and finds the truths that are hidden alike by daylight and dreams. Things we are not ready to know abide in that place, awaiting that unguarded frame of mind.
Silence can ask all the questions, where the tongue is prone to ask only the wrong one.
I don’t understand. You are ill? No. Just stupid. Ah. Nothing new there. Well, you haven’t died from that so far. But sometimes it has been a near thing.

Change comes upon us again, Changer. I can feel it at the edge of the horizon, almost smell it. It is like a bigger predator come into our hunting territory. Do not you feel it? I feel nothing. But he heard the lie. He sighed out a heavy breath.
“It doesn’t matter who a man’s father is. Your parents made a child, but it’s up to you to make the man you’ll be.”

We moved for a space in wolf time, in the contentment of the present, not worrying about what had passed or what was to come. That evening remains for me always a moment to cherish, as golden and fragrant as brandy in crystal glasses.
“When you cut pieces from the truth to avoid sounding like a fool, you end up sounding like a moron instead.”
The truth, I discovered, is a tree that grows as a man gains access to experience. A child sees the acorn of his daily life, but a man looks back on the oak.
I felt my life as Fitz was like footprints on a dusty floor, already being swept aside and overtrodden by others.
You’ve made me look like an idiot. That wasn’t hard.

Little brother, do not treat me as if I am already dead, or dying. If you see me that way, then I would rather truly be dead. You steal the now of my life away, when you constantly fear that tomorrow will bring my death. Your fears clutch cold at me and snatch all my pleasure in the day’s warmth from me.
Snarling, I looked down at my stalker. I looked into my own eyes looking into my own eyes looking into my own eyes—
The Skill is infinitely large, and yet intimately small. It is as large as the world and the sky above it, and as small as a man’s secret heart.
Wait for you? Not likely! I’ve always had to run ahead of you and show you the way.

“You are not the cat. The cat died. You are a man, and you must go on living. The blessing of Old Blood is that they share their lives with us. The curse is that those lives are seldom as long as our own.”
So grief has always seemed to me, a time of waiting not for the hurt to pass, but to become accustomed to it.
